elements.element: Customer may assign without Vendor consent to an Affiliate
elements.evidence: "Licensee may assign this Agreement, without Licensor's consent, to an Affiliate"

elements.element: Customer may assign without consent to a successor in a merger, acquisition or sale of substantially all assets
elements.evidence: "or to a successor in a merger, acquisition or sale of substantially all of its assets"; consent gate opened by "Except as provided below,"

elements.element: Vendor may not assign without Customer's prior written consent
elements.evidence: "Licensor may not assign this Agreement without Licensee's prior written consent"

elements.element: Customer's consent to Vendor assignment not to be unreasonably withheld
Vendor may never assign to a Customer competitor
elements.evidence: "and in no event to a competitor of Licensee"

elements.element: No Vendor termination (or automatic termination of licences) on Customer's change of control
elements.evidence: "shall continue in full force and effect whether or not, prior to the occurrence of such Change of Control, Licensor has consented"

elements.element: Mutual right to assign to successors
elements.evidence: Vendor side is a consent gate, not a right: "Licensor may not assign this Agreement without Licensee's prior written consent"
No notice mechanic appears in the inserted sentences

elements.element: Consent for other assignments not unreasonably withheld

reasons: All six atomic preferred elements are satisfied: Customer-side affiliate and successor carve-out from the consent gate, Vendor assignment gated on Customer's consent with a reasonableness standard, an absolute competitor bar, and removal of the automatic termination of the Agreement and licences on Customer's Change of Control.

Edits are surgical: a four-word carve-out lead-in, one inserted two-sentence assignment provision for the absent Customer/Vendor assignment rights, deletion of the cross-reference that would have subordinated the new carve-out to the Change of Control section, and an operator-level flip of "automatically terminate unless" to "continue in full force and effect whether or not". No preferred-only extras, no new exceptions, no whole-clause rewrite.

Note (rationale-level, not a deviation): the residual "provided that Licensor will not unreasonably withhold its consent" and the deemed-reasonable-withholding sentence in Article XX(a) are now inoperative surplusage since consent no longer conditions continuation; they create no contradiction but could be struck for tidiness. The Change of Control and Control definitions and all unrelated terms remain intact and effective.
The clause as redlined sits at the preferred position, so no fallback (mutual successor assignment with written notice) analysis is required; it is not met and need not be.
